newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian government backs low-paid pay rise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian government backs low-paid pay rise.

text.p: Australia's federal government will back a pay rise of A$8 a week for each of the next three years for low-paid workers in a submission to the Industrial Relations Commission, Prime Minister John Howard said on Sunday.
Howard said the government's support for the wage rise followed the recent 0.5 percentage point cut in official interest rates by the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA).

"Through the saftey net adjustment we are now protecting the most low paid in our community and we are doing it in a way which won't exacerbate wage pressure and thereby threaten the very low level of inflation that we now have," Howard said in a
speech to the Victoria state Liberal Party council in Geelong.
The government's proposal would apply to workers paid less than average weekly ordinary time earnings.
In response, Australian Council of Trade Unions president Jennie George said it showed the government cared little for low paid workers.

The peak union body is seeking a safety net increase of A$20 a week and also wants to boost minimum wages by lifting entry level award pay rates to a minimum of A$12 an hour during the next three years.
The Industrial Relations Commission is scheduled to begin hearings on the wage case early next month.
